data.long_meaning: From the Greek word hepsibō, meaning 'dedicated to God'. In the Bible, there is a woman named Hepsibah mentioned in Jeremiah 31:22. The name Hepsiba carries the meaning “Dedicated to God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Hepsiba usually hope their child will grow to embody dedicated to god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing devotion and faithfulness to God.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hepsiba total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hepsiba has its roots in Greek mythology and Biblical history. In ancient Greece, Hepsibō was a name dedicated to the god Apollo, signifying dedication to the divine. In the Bible, Hepsibah is a woman who represents hope and restoration, as she is mentioned in Jeremiah 31:22 in relation to the return of Israelites to their homeland after exile.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Hepsiba holds deep spiritual significance as it is a reminder of dedication to God and the promise of hope and restoration. It can serve as a reminder for individuals to remain committed to their faith and trust in God's plan, even during difficult times. The name also represents the transformative power of God, as seen in the biblical reference to Hepsibah being mentioned in the context of the Israelites returning home after exile.

biblical_reference.note: Hepsibah was the daughter of Abitur and the wife of Barzillai. She lived in Ribbonah. When David fled from Absalom, she took care of him and his men.

historical_references.reference: In ancient Greek, Hepsiba is derived from the word "heptos", meaning seven, and "bia", meaning life.
historical_references.context: In ancient Greek mythology, Hepsiba was the name of a nymph who was associated with the number seven.
